name: Scandinavian Defense: Anderssen Counterattack, Orthodox Attack
description: Black's queen to a5 develops actively, and after d4 and White's center, Black compensates with piece pressure via Nc6 and Bb4.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Blackburne Gambit
description: Black sacrifices both d5 and c6 pawns, gaining rapid knight development to c6 with immediate tactical threats against White's center.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Blackburne-Kloosterboer Gambit
description: Black plays c6 attacking the d5 pawn, sacrificing material to create rapid compensation through piece activity and central counterplay.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Boehnke Gambit
description: Black sacrifices d5 and e5 pawns consecutively, rapidly developing the bishop to e6 with active piece play and tactical opportunities.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Bronstein Variation
description: Queen retreats to d6 instead of a5, with a6 preventing Bb5+ checks while maintaining centralized queen control and flexibility.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Classical Variation
description: After d4, Black develops methodically with Nf6 and Bf5, keeping the queen actively placed while building solid piece coordination.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Grünfeld Variation
description: White aggressively plays g4 after Ne5, attacking Black's bishop on f5 and seizing kingside space immediately.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Gubinsky-Melts Defense
description: Queen goes to d6 from the start, centralizing rather than the rim and supporting flexible center development options.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Icelandic-Palme Gambit
description: Black develops Nf6 and e6 attacking the d5 pawn, while White supports it with c4, establishing a solid pawn structure.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Kádas Gambit
description: Black creates immediate threats with Nf6, c6, and e5, mounting continuous pressure on White's central pawn structure.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Kiel Variation
description: Black takes d5 with the knight and plays Nb4, forcing White's c4 pawn advance while displacing the knight actively.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Kloosterboer Gambit
description: Black sacrifices d5 and c6, then plays e5, generating multiple central threats and tactical complications immediately.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Lasker Variation
description: Black develops Bg4, and White responds h3 attacking the bishop, establishing a solid defensive foundation against piece pressure.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Main Line, Leonhardt Gambit
description: White aggressively plays b4, attacking the queen directly and sacrificing material for sharp tactical complications and initiative.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Main Line, Mieses Variation
description: Standard setup with d4 and Nf6, establishing White's central control while Black develops methodically with piece coordination.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Marshall Variation
description: Black takes d5 with the knight instead of the queen, prioritizing active piece play over immediate material recovery tactics.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Mieses-Kotroc Variation
description: Queen captures on d5 immediately, setting up the core position for the Scandinavian's main transformations and tactical play.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Modern Variation
description: Black plays Nf6 without recapturing, and d4 establishes the center, creating dynamic piece activity and tactical flexibility.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Modern Variation, Gipslis Variation
description: Black develops Bg4 creating immediate pin threats against the knight, generating rapid tactical pressure and tempo.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Modern Variation, Wing Gambit
description: Black fianchettoes with g6 and challenges c4 with b5, creating tactical complications and aggressive space play.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Panov Transfer
description: White plays c4 instead of d4, and Black responds c6, transposing toward Slav-like structures with dynamic piece play.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Portuguese Gambit
description: Black develops the bishop to g4 immediately, pinning the knight and generating rapid tactical threats and tempo.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Portuguese Gambit, Banker Variation
description: Black retreats Bf5 and White consolidates with c4 after f3, establishing a solid center and piece coordination.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Portuguese Gambit, Classical Variation
description: White develops Nf3 naturally facing the immediate pin from Bg4, establishing piece activity without rash kingside advances.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Portuguese Gambit, Correspondence Refutation
description: White aggressively pushes g4 after f3, attacking the bishop and seizing kingside space with sharp tactical intent.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Portuguese Gambit, Elbow Variation
description: White checks with Bb5+ forcing c6, a forcing sequence that restricts Black's piece development and bishop placement.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Portuguese Gambit, Jadoul Variation
description: Multiple sharp developments with Bb5+, f3, c4 creating a complex position requiring precise tactical defense from Black.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Portuguese Gambit, Lusophobe Variation
description: White retreats Bb5 to e2 after the check, a passive approach that limits piece coordination and attacking pressure.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Portuguese Gambit, Melbourne Shuffle Variation
description: White develops Nc3 after f3 and Bf5, building central support and piece coordination with moderate pressure.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Portuguese Gambit, Wuss Variation
description: White plays Be2 instead of f3, a passive approach avoiding direct confrontation with Black's g4 bishop.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Richter Variation
description: Black fianchettoes with g6, creating a solid kingside structure with lateral pressure and flexible piece placement.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Schiller-Pytel Variation
description: Queen to d6 with c6 support establishes a methodical defensive structure against White's central play with d4.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Schiller-Pytel Variation, Modern Variation
description: White plays Bc4 and Nge2, Black develops c6 and Bf5, with queen to b4 creating tactical threats and complexity.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Valencian Variation
description: Queen retreats to d8 immediately, a conservative approach keeping the queen safe while maintaining flexible piece options.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Valencian Variation, Ilundain Variation
description: Black develops methodically with c6 and Nf6, supporting the center and establishing a solid defensive foundation.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Valencian Variation, Main Line
description: After Qd8, d4, Nf6, Black develops Bg4 pinning the knight and creating immediate tactical pressure.

name: Scandinavian Defense: Zilbermints Gambit
description: White plays b4 immediately as an unusual gambit, sacrificing space for rapid kingside attacking play opportunities.

name: Van Geet Opening: Grünfeld Defense
description: Black plays e5 after Nxe4, controlling the center and creating active piece play from the opening moves.

name: Alekhine Defense: Brooklyn Variation
description: Black retreats Ng8, an unusual retreat that abandons piece activity for dubious and passive defensive ideas.

name: Alekhine Defense: Brooklyn Variation, Everglades Variation
description: Black plays f5 attacking e5 from the Ng8 retreat, a counterattacking tactical idea attempting compensation.

name: Alekhine Defense: Buckley Attack
description: White plays Na3, an unusual knight placement creating awkward piece coordination and weak central pawn control.

name: Alekhine Defense: Hunt Variation, Lasker Simul Gambit
description: White pushes c4-c5, forcing the knight around repeatedly while developing Bc4 and Nc3 for attacking chances.

name: Alekhine Defense: Hunt Variation, Matsukevich Gambit
description: After trading Nxc3, White recaptures with d-pawn, Bg5 pins and develops, controlling central squares firmly.

name: Alekhine Defense: Hunt Variation, Mikenas Gambit
description: White plays Nxd5 exd5 Bxd5, maintaining strong central control with the bishop after knight trades.

name: Alekhine Defense: Kmoch Variation
description: White plays Bc4-Bb3, Black responds c5, creating central counterplay against White's moderate piece coordination.

name: Alekhine Defense: Krejcik Variation
description: White plays Bc4 immediately, an alternative developing approach creating immediate threats on the f7-e6 diagonal.

name: Alekhine Defense: Krejcik Variation, Krejcik Gambit
description: White sacrifices f7 with check after Nxe4, a tactical gambit trying to generate rapid attacking play.

name: Alekhine Defense: Maróczy Variation
description: White plays d3, a solid quiet approach avoiding sharp tactics and building a measured, methodical position.

name: Alekhine Defense: Mokele Mbembe
description: Black plays Ne4, a solid system attacking the e5 pawn and centralizing the knight aggressively.

name: Alekhine Defense: Mokele Mbembe, Modern Line
description: Black plays f6 supporting e4, attacking e5, and opening tactical lines for active piece play.
